The middle of the two-port network is labeled [Z]. The arrow of the left-port current I1 points into the network, and the port voltage V1 is positive at the top and negative at the bottom. On the right side, port 2 is connected to a load ZL, the arrow of the port current I2 also points into the network, and the port voltage V2 is positive at the top and negative at the bottom. Reasoning: the given impedance parameters are V1 = 40I1 + 60I2, V2 = 60I1 + 120I2. To make the load obtain maximum power, let ZL be equal to the Thevenin resistance seen looking into port 2. When finding this resistance, set the 120 V independent voltage source to zero, that is, replace the voltage source with a short circuit, so the 10 Ω resistor is connected across the two ends of port 1. According to the current direction in the figure, the 10 Ω resistor externally connected to port 1 gives V1 = -10I1. Substituting into V1 = 40I1 + 60I2 gives -10I1 = 40I1 + 60I2, so -50I1 = 60I2, I1 = -1.2I2. Then substituting into V2 = 60I1 + 120I2 gives V2 = 60(-1.2I2) + 120I2 = -72I2 + 120I2 = 48I2. Therefore the equivalent resistance seen looking into port 2 is Rth = V2/I2 = 48 Ω. At maximum power transfer, ZL = Rth = 48 Ω.

The middle of the two-port network is labeled [Z]. The arrow of the left-port current I1 points into the network, and the port voltage V1 is positive at the top and negative at the bottom. On the right side, port 2 is connected to a load ZL, the arrow of the port current I2 also points into the network, and the port voltage V2 is positive at the top and negative at the bottom.

Reasoning: the given impedance parameters are V1 = 40I1 + 60I2, V2 = 60I1 + 120I2. To make the load obtain maximum power, let ZL be equal to the Thevenin resistance seen looking into port 2. When finding this resistance, set the 120 V independent voltage source to zero, that is, replace the voltage source with a short circuit, so the 10 Ω resistor is connected across the two ends of port 1. According to the current direction in the figure, the 10 Ω resistor externally connected to port 1 gives V1 = -10I1. Substituting into V1 = 40I1 + 60I2 gives -10I1 = 40I1 + 60I2, so -50I1 = 60I2, I1 = -1.2I2. Then substituting into V2 = 60I1 + 120I2 gives V2 = 60(-1.2I2) + 120I2 = -72I2 + 120I2 = 48I2. Therefore the equivalent resistance seen looking into port 2 is Rth = V2/I2 = 48 Ω. At maximum power transfer, ZL = Rth = 48 Ω.
